rationale:
Evidence from iteration 0: every trial on all three development tracks went off track (20 of 20 per track, finish rate 0). Progress was only 0.04 to 0.12 and each run logged one line-loss event. max_error is about 0.061 m, just above the off-track limit of max(0.06, 0.03) = 0.06 m, so the robot drifts off the tape early and does not recover. The fault is control authority and damping, not geometry. At base_speed 1.6 the loop cannot correct errors fast enough, and kp 3.0 with kd 0.3 is too soft to hold the line through bends.

Changes: (1) base_speed 1.6 to 1.2, so the robot has time to correct on bends; (2) kp 3.0 to 5.0, for stronger steering on the 25 mm tape; (3) kd 0.3 to 0.8, to damp the faster corrective swings that caused oscillation; (4) ki 0.05 to 0.02, to limit integral windup on long bends; (5) line_loss kept at last_direction, since it is the most reasonable recovery when the line is lost. Geometry is unchanged so the controller change is isolated.

Expected result: no off-track ends on the oval and s-bend, max_error below about 0.04 m, and at least some finishes on the slalom. Completion time will be longer than the 3 s target (about 1.2 m/s average would give roughly 4 s), so completion, not time, is the first goal. Hypotheses: (a) the robot now stays within 0.04 m of the centre line; (b) line_loss_events drops to 0; (c) steering_oscillation rises only modestly with kd 0.8. Next steps depend on the result: if it completes with margin, raise base_speed in 0.2 steps; if oscillation is high, raise kd before kp.
